definitions.guardrail: Top and Bottom are focal-election purchase-size strata, not observed wealth, ideology, sophistication, or institutional status.

methods.amount_network: For active wallet u, p_ui=x_ui/sum_j x_uj and v_u=sum_j x_uj. W_ij=sum_u v_u p_ui p_uj / sum_u v_u; diagonal removed.
methods.equal_wallet_network: W_ij=(1/n) sum_u p_ui p_uj over active wallets; each wallet has the same coefficient before projection and dollar-size weighting is removed. After diagonal removal, more diversified wallets contribute more off-diagonal mass.
methods.binary_network: W_ij=(1/n) sum_u 1[x_ui>0]1[x_uj>0] over active wallets; diagonal removed.
methods.comparison: All networks use the same 22 subjects. Each edge vector is normalized to unit total before JSD/cosine comparison. Dominant-edge overlap uses identical top-22 and top-40 edge budgets.
methods.clustering: Average linkage on the mean of six Jensen-Shannon distances: three subject profiles and three subject-edge representations. Candidate labels do not enter the clustering objective.
methods.community: Weighted Louvain at resolution 1 with 200 seeds; best modularity and mean pairwise adjusted Rand index report optimization stability. This is a sensitivity audit, not evidence of political communities.
methods.uncertainty: Within-cohort nonparametric wallet bootstrap (1999 replicates). The reported interval is for Bottom-pair JSD minus Top-pair JSD; positive values indicate stronger Top-pair convergence.
methods.dominant_wallet_sensitivity: Recompute dollar-weighted profiles, edges, and top-five hubs after removing the largest one, top 1%, or top 5% October spenders within each cohort. This is an influence analysis; the September cohort definitions remain unchanged.
